rootsNote: sourceRoot is the repository root, spelled relative to this directory because vacuity-check's find_root() tries the campaign directory FIRST: a literal "." resolves to planning/test-campaign, and the census then reports 4 of 8 providers resolved by matching symbols against this directory's own bin/*.py. Measured 2026-08-27. The root has to be the repository because the product ships TWO production trees — Swift under app/Sources and TypeScript under src/ — the instrument takes one root, and four providers (REQ-021, REQ-024, REQ-025, REQ-026) name a file in each. Under app/Sources those four resolve to nothing; under the repository all eight named providers resolve, every one of them by PATH rather than by symbol. WHAT THE CHOICE LEAVES UNMEASURED: the production index is 449 files, of which 393 are app/Sources and 15 are src/. The other 41 are pipeline gates, build scripts and evidence probes under planning/, scripts/, design/ and app/Scripts — SKIP_DIRS and TEST_MARKERS are module constants and cannot be configured away. They cost nothing today because no provider falls through to the symbol half, and they are a live weakness the day one does: a future provider could resolve on a symbol that exists only in a gate script. If the campaign directory ever moves, "../.." lands on a different existing directory and the providers stop resolving — the census goes red rather than quiet, which is the failure direction to want. testRoot is app rather than app/Tests, so the blind pass reads the five MCPRouterIOSTests/MCPRouterIOSUITests files as well as the 252 under app/Tests; and rather than the repository, which would hand the pass 20 campaign scripts under planning/test-campaign/bin plus the eight vendored instrument scripts and have the checker examine itself. Two things it does not reach: src/ has NO tests at all, and scripts/e2e*.mjs is invisible because .mjs is not in the pass's suffix set. Six production files ride along under app because Inspector contains the substring spec (ActivityInspector, EvalsInspector, ServerInspector, ServerInspectorControls, ServerInspectorSections, SkillInspector) — DEF-055's structural finding, still live. A blindVocabulary IS now declared, by K4 on 2026-08-29, and the sentence this replaces was reasoning from the reader side only. DEF-055's argument -- that adding this codebase's read idioms lowers the count without improving what the pass knows -- still stands and is why the reader list stops short of the assertion macro. It said nothing about the MUTATOR side, which is where the pass was blind: measured on this corpus, the nine snake_case defaults find 3 mutating call sites in 2282 test bodies where the fitted list finds 481, so the recall the campaign was declining to publish a number from was 3 of 481. See blindVocabulary.note.

swiftui.attachedBy: NOT ATTACHED, and the distinction is this lane's whole content. It hosts the product's own SwiftUI views in an NSHostingView inside a process whose activation policy is `.prohibited` and whose window is never ordered in. It does NOT claim MCPRouter.app was running and drawn — that is macos-glass's claim, and macos-glass proves it by axkit attaching to a CGWindowID the launched pid owns. What this lane witnesses is narrower and is stated as such: the hierarchy under measurement is compiled from app/Sources/MCPRouterUI rather than mocked, it laid out, and it painted. The in-view recorder (MCPRouterUI/Measure/Measured.swift, compiled only under MEASURE) reports resolved frames from inside the views themselves, because an NSHostingView hosting a real hierarchy has exactly one AppKit subview and walking it from outside the process returns nothing. A run whose recorder found no nodes exits 3 rather than writing an empty dump and reading as agreement.
swiftui.captureChannel: NSHostingView.cacheDisplay(in:to:) -> NSBitmapImageRep -> PNG, off the view's own backing store. Not screencapture and not ScreenCaptureKit: nothing is photographed off the display, so no window can occlude the subject and there is no screen to take. G17 samples the frontmost application once a second for the whole of its run and asserts that neither MeasureDump nor the router ever appears in the sample (planning/test-campaign/evidence/g17-document/frontmost.txt) — a stronger statement than comparing the frontmost app before and after, which a third-party application stealing focus mid-run turns into a false red.

blindVocabulary.note:
Declared 2026-08-29 by K4 against the corpus at `testRoot` (app), measured at `83e5380`. `only` is true because the nine shipped defaults are snake_case for a Rust/RPC shape and this is camelCase Swift: unioned in they contribute nothing except `restart`, which is the verb that produced all three of the findings the campaign could not adjudicate.

HOW THE MUTATOR LIST WAS DERIVED, in two stages, the second of which is a judgement and is recorded as one. Stage 1 is mechanical: every call verb in the corpus was counted three ways -- implicit-member expressions (`.reset(.clearPlacard)`, DEF-055 cause 3), method calls on a receiver, and the verb's own `func` declaration line (DEF-055 cause 4, the body slice starting at the declaration so a test whose name begins with a mutator matches itself) -- and a verb is kept only where method calls are at least half its sites and `func` declarations at most a quarter. That rule alone removes `restart` (1 method call, 3 declarations, of 5 sites), `reset` (19 of 62 declarations), `clear`, `delete`, `shutdown`, `dismiss` and `approve` on the declaration test, and `install`, `select`, `open`, `close`, `refuse`, `rename` and `moveItem` for not being method-dominant. Stage 2 drops five verbs the rule kept -- `append`, `run`, `apply`, `lock`, `unlock` -- whose receiver in this corpus is a local collection or test scaffolding rather than the system under test.

WHAT THE READER LIST DELIBERATELY OMITS, because it is the tempting shortcut and it would be rule 10. `expect` and `require` are swift-testing's assertion macros and appear 5781 and 383 times; declaring either a reader would mark every test that asserts after mutating as re-reading and collapse the count to near zero without the pass having learned anything. `contains`, `filter` and `map` are transforms over a value already read and are omitted for the same reason. The list holds names that denote reading state, property-style names included, because the instrument's reader test carries no word boundary and a false reader match suppresses a finding, which is the safe direction.

WHAT IT MEASURES, all four figures over the same 2282 test bodies so the vocabulary's effect is visible rather than buried. Defaults: mutating=3 re-read=0 blind=3. Fitted mutators with no readers at all: mutating=481 blind=481. Fitted mutators with the ten tightest readers only: re-read=271 blind=210. Fitted mutators with this full reader list: re-read=370 blind=111. The reader list therefore suppresses 370 of 481, and the 99 between 210 and 111 is what the looser half of it costs -- stated, not hidden.

THE 111 IS A WORKLIST AND THE CAMPAIGN STILL CLAIMS NO BLIND NUMBER. DEF-055 measured 0 of 3 precision on the previous population and its structural causes are not withdrawn: the pass still examines every `func` rather than every `@Test`, its helper exclusion is still file-scoped, and a mutator in a `defer` block still reads as source-early. `bin/blind-vocabulary-arm.py` arms this vocabulary two ways on every run.
